newsitem.title: ITALY: PRESS DIGEST - Italy - Wednesday, January 29.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Italy - Wednesday, January 29.

text.p: Following are some of the top headlines in leading Italian newspapers.
* Police in Palermo discovered a plot to kill Giancarlo Caselli, one of Italy's leading anti-Mafia prosecutors (all).

* Prime Minister Romano Prodi said it might be "useful" to bring forward the 1998 budget to earlier in the year. Leftist PDS leader Massimo D'Alema said he backs the proposal but there must be a broad agreement with the opposition (all).
* The lira lost ground against the mark and the dollar after Prodi said the current rate exchange was "a bit too strong" (all).
* In October 1996 big companies' employment fell 3.5 percent year-on-year (all).
* Shares in information technology group Olivetti tumbled with investors fearing the worst from preliminary 1996 results due today (all).
* Talks are due to resume today between metalworkers' trade unions and employers to try and reach an agreement over a long-running pay dispute (all).

* In an interview, hard-left Communist Refoundation leader Fausto Bertinotti reaffirms the state should maintain a 51 percent stake in telecom holding Stet. Bertinotti also said there should be "only one budget in 1997" (Sole 24 Ore).
Reuters has not verified these stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
